familias/religiones:religiones-del-antig.texto: Religions of the ancient Near East

familias/religiones:religion-grecorroman.texto: Groups the Greek and Roman religions, which gradually became identified with each other (Zeus with Jupiter, Athena with Minerva) and coexisted throughout the Hellenistic and Roman Mediterranean.

familias/religiones:politeismo-iranio/no.texto: Includes Elamite religion, which is not Iranian: it is grouped here because the sources for the region treat them together.

familias/religiones:religiones-originari.texto: Indigenous religions of the Río de la Plata

familias/idiomas:sumerio/nota.texto: Language isolate: it has no known relatives.

familias/idiomas:elamita/nota.texto: A language isolate according to most specialists.

familias/idiomas:romances/nota.texto: The languages that developed from spoken Latin.

familias/idiomas:persa/nota.texto: Old Persian (Achaemenid), Middle Persian or Pahlavi (Sasanian) and Modern Persian.

familias/idiomas:lenguas-indigenas-de-am.texto: Not a family: it groups many families with no demonstrated relationship to one another.

familias/religiones:arrianismo/nota.texto: Christianity that denied that the Son was of the same substance as the Father; it was the faith of the Goths, Vandals and Lombards until their conversion to Catholicism.

familias/religiones:catarismo/nota.texto: Dualist movement of Languedoc and northern Italy, crushed by the Albigensian Crusade and the Inquisition.

familias/religiones:husitismo/nota.texto: Reformed church of Bohemia that followed Jan Hus; its moderate branch, the Utraquists, was the majority in the 15th century.

familias/religiones:paganismo-europeo/no.texto: Groups religions with no direct relationship to one another: the Germanic, Slavic, Baltic and Celtic religions, and that of the Hungarians before their Christianization.

familias/religiones:paganismo-baltico/no.texto: The Lithuanians were the last pagan people of Europe: their grand duke Jogaila was baptized in 1386, and Samogitia in 1413.

familias/religiones:protestantismo/nota.texto: Lutherans, Reformed (Calvinists), Anglicans and the other churches born of the 16th-century Reformation.

familias/culturas:andalusi/nota.texto: The Arab and Islamic culture of al-Andalus, created by Arabs, Berbers and a majority of Hispanic converts (muwallads).

familias/culturas:celta/nota.texto: Groups together the peoples who spoke Celtic languages. The Greeks called them keltoi and galatai and the Romans Celtae and Galli; the Irish and the Welsh were not called Celts until Edward Lhuyd (1707) used the name for their languages, and whether ancient Celtic culture was a unity is debated (James, 1999; Collis, 2003).

familias/idiomas:nordico/nota.texto: Includes its medieval successors: Old Icelandic, Old Norwegian, Old Swedish and Old Danish.

familias/idiomas:ingles/nota.texto: Old English (Anglo-Saxon) until the 12th century, then Middle English.

familias/idiomas:aleman/nota.texto: Old and Middle High German, and Low German in the north.

familias/idiomas:irlandes/nota.texto: Includes Scottish Gaelic, which split from Middle Irish at the end of the Middle Ages.

familias/idiomas:eslavo-eclesiastico/not.texto: Written and liturgical language of the Orthodox Slavs, created by Cyril and Methodius on the basis of the speech of Thessalonica.

familias/idiomas:eslavo-oriental/nota.texto: Ancestor of Russian, Ukrainian and Belarusian.

familias/idiomas:eslavas-meridionales/no.texto: Bulgarian, Macedonian, Serbian, Croatian and Slovene.

familias/idiomas:finicas/nota.texto: Estonian, Finnish, Karelian and other languages of the eastern Baltic.

familias/idiomas:vasco/nota.texto: Language isolate: the only surviving language of western Europe that predates the Indo-European languages.

familias/idiomas:hebreo/nota.texto: In the Middle Ages, the written language of Jewish liturgy, law, poetry and philosophy.

familias/religiones:samaritanismo/nota.texto: Israelite religion with its own Pentateuch and its sanctuary on Mount Gerizim, not in Jerusalem.

familias/religiones:druzos/nota.texto: Born in the 11th century from the Fatimid Ismailism of Egypt; since 1043 it has not accepted converts.

familias/religiones:ismailismo/nota.texto: Shia branch to which the Fatimid caliphs of Cairo and the Nizaris of Alamut and Masyaf belonged.

familias/religiones:maronitas/nota.texto: Syriac church of Lebanon, united with Rome since the time of the Crusades.

familias/religiones:miafisismo/nota.texto: Churches that rejected the Council of Chalcedon (451): the Syriac, Armenian, Coptic and Ethiopian churches.

familias/religiones:religion-arabe-preis.texto: Tribal cults of gods such as Hubal, Al-Lat, Al-Uzza and Manat, with sanctuaries such as the Kaaba in Mecca.

familias/religiones:ibadismo/nota.texto: The only surviving branch of the Kharijites; the majority in Oman.

familias/culturas:pampeano-patagonica/no.texto: Peoples of the Pampas and Patagonia
A geographic grouping of nomadic hunters, later mounted: Tehuelches (Aonikenk), Gününa Küna or Puelches, Pampas and others. It is not a linguistic unit.

familias/culturas:mapuche/nota.texto: Includes the Mapudungun-speaking groups of the Pampas and Patagonia, such as the Ranqueles, Pehuenches and the people of Salinas Grandes.

familias/culturas:fueguina/nota.texto: Selk’nam, Haush, Yaganes and Kawésqar: two peoples of mainland hunters and two of canoeists.

familias/culturas:chaquena/nota.texto: Peoples speaking Guaycurú languages (Qom, Mocoví, Pilagá, Abipón), Mataco-Mataguayan languages (Wichí, Chorote, Nivaclé) and other families.

familias/culturas:guarani/nota.texto: Includes the Chiriguanos or ava guaraní of the Andean foothills.

familias/culturas:afrodescendiente/nota.texto: Descendants of enslaved Africans brought to the Americas.

familias/culturas:italiana/nota.texto: For regions of massive Italian immigration, such as the Río de la Plata from 1870.

familias/idiomas:chon/nota.texto: Tehuelche (aonek’o ajen), gününa yajüch, Selk’nam and Haush. The relationship of gününa yajüch to the others is disputed.

familias/culturas:paleoindia/nota.texto: The first settlers of America, late Pleistocene hunter-gatherers (Clovis, Folsom, Monte Verde, Lagoa Santa and others).

familias/culturas:paleoesquimal/nota.texto: Saqqaq, Independence, Pre-Dorset and Dorset in the eastern Arctic; Denbigh and Choris in Alaska. Ancient DNA shows them to be a population distinct from the Thule.

familias/culturas:esquimo-aleutiana/nota.texto: Inuit, Yupik and Aleuts. “Eskimo” is an exonym that many Inuit in Canada and Greenland reject; it is still used in Alaska.

familias/culturas:inuit/nota.texto: Includes their Thule ancestors, the Inupiat of Alaska, the Inuvialuit, the Inuit of Canada and Labrador, and the Kalaallit of Greenland.

familias/culturas:yupik/nota.texto: Yupik of southwestern Alaska and St. Lawrence Island, and Alutiiq or Sugpiaq of Kodiak, the Alaska Peninsula and Prince William Sound.

familias/culturas:atabascana/nota.texto: Includes the Athabaskans of Alaska and northwestern Canada, and the Apaches and Navajos of the Southwest.

familias/culturas:iroquesa/nota.texto: The nations of the Iroquois Confederacy, the Huron or Wendat, the Neutrals, the Erie, the Susquehannock and, in the Southeast, the Cherokee.

familias/culturas:woodland/nota.texto: Adena, Hopewell and other eastern woodland cultures between 1000 BC and AD 1000: pottery, burial mounds and early cultivation.

familias/culturas:misisipiana/nota.texto: Agricultural chiefdoms with earthen platforms between 800 and 1600, from Cahokia to Moundville, Etowah and Spiro.

familias/culturas:pueblos-del-sudeste/no.texto: Muskogee (Creeks), Seminoles, Choctaws, Chickasaws, Cherokees, Natchez, Caddo, Timucua and others.

familias/culturas:llanera/nota.texto: Farmers of the Missouri villages and bison hunters; from the 18th century, horse-riding peoples such as the Lakota, Cheyenne, Comanche and Blackfoot.

familias/culturas:costa-noroeste/nota.texto: Tlingit, Haida, Tsimshian, Kwakwaka’wakw, Nuu-chah-nulth, Coast Salish, Chinook and others: sedentary fishing peoples with ranks, slaves and the potlatch.

familias/culturas:meseta/nota.texto: Nez Perce, Yakama, Umatilla, Cayuse, Interior Salish, Kutenai, Klamath and others, between the Cascades and the Rockies.

familias/culturas:oasisamericana/nota.texto: Farmers of the desert of the southwestern United States and northwestern Mexico: Hohokam, Mogollon, Ancestral Puebloans, Paquimé and their descendants.

familias/culturas:pueblo/nota.texto: Hopi, Zuni and the Rio Grande Pueblos (Keres, Tewa, Tiwa, Towa), descendants of the Ancestral Puebloans.

familias/culturas:aridoamericana/nota.texto: Hunter-gatherers of north-central Mexico (the “Chichimecas” of Nahua and Spanish sources) and farmers of the sierra and the northwestern coast.

familias/culturas:nahua/nota.texto: Includes the Mexica, Acolhua, Tlaxcalans, Pipil and Nicarao.

familias/culturas:arahuaca/nota.texto: Peoples speaking Arawakan languages in the Antilles, the Guianas, the Orinoco and Amazonia.

familias/culturas:taina/nota.texto: Farmers of the Greater Antilles and the Bahamas (the Lucayans) at the time of Columbus’s arrival.

familias/culturas:caribes/nota.texto: Kari’na of the mainland and Kalinago of the Lesser Antilles; the latter spoke an Arawakan language.

familias/culturas:istmo-colombiana/nota.texto: Peoples speaking Chibchan languages and their neighbors, from Honduras to northern Colombia: Cuevas, Ngäbe, Bribri, Kuna, Tairona, Zenú and Muisca.

familias/culturas:tupi/nota.texto: Tupinambá, Tupiniquim, Potiguara and other Tupi peoples of the coast and rivers of Brazil; the Guaraní have their own family.

familias/culturas:ye/nota.texto: Kaingang, Xokleng, Xavante, Xerente, Kayapó, Timbira and other peoples speaking Ye languages; in the broad sense, speakers of the macro-Ye languages, such as the Botocudo. The Tupi called all peoples who did not speak Tupi tapuias, many of them Ye.

familias/culturas:amazonica/nota.texto: Not a single unit: it groups hundreds of peoples of the Amazon basin, from many language families.

familias/culturas:brasilena/nota.texto: A Luso-Brazilian society formed by Portuguese, Africans, Indigenous people and their descendants, and later by European and Asian immigrants.

familias/idiomas:inuit/nota.texto: A dialect continuum from Alaska to Greenland, a legacy of the Thule expansion some 700 years ago.

familias/idiomas:na-dene/nota.texto: Athabaskan, Eyak and Tlingit; Haida, which Sapir included, is now considered an isolate.

familias/idiomas:atabascanas/nota.texto: Includes Navajo and the Apache languages of the Southwest.

familias/idiomas:otomangues/nota.texto: Zapotec, Mixtec, Otomí, Mazatec, Chinantec, Chorotega and others.

familias/idiomas:macro-ye/nota.texto: The Ye stock is secure; the inclusion of other families in Macro-Ye is debated.

familias/idiomas:misumalpas/nota.texto: Miskito, Sumo (Mayangna) and the extinct Matagalpa.

familias/idiomas:niger-congo/nota.texto: The languages of most enslaved Africans brought to America: Kimbundu, Kikongo, Yoruba, Fon, Ewe, Akan and others.

familias/religiones:iglesia-nativa-ameri.texto: Combines the ritual use of peyote with Christian elements; it was formally established in Oklahoma in 1918.

familias/religiones:casa-larga/nota.texto: Founded by the Seneca prophet Handsome Lake around 1799.

familias/religiones:religiones-afroameri.texto: Haitian Vodou, santería, candomblé, umbanda, obeah, winti and others, of African origin and with Catholic and Indigenous elements.

familias/idiomas:preindoeuropeas/nota.texto: The languages of Europe's Neolithic farmers, before the arrival of the Indo-European ones. They left no texts: they are used on the map for whatever lies before any documented language, and their traces are sought in place names and loanwords, with much-disputed theories (Vennemann's “Vasconic”, for example, has little support).

familias/idiomas:galo/nota.texto: Celtic language of Gaul, written from the 3rd century BC in Greek letters and then Latin ones; it died out between the 5th and 6th centuries.

familias/idiomas:lepontico/nota.texto: The oldest written Celtic language (6th century BC), from the lakes of northern Italy. Whether it is a separate language or an archaic Gaulish is debated.

familias/idiomas:celtibero/nota.texto: Celtic language of the eastern Meseta of the Iberian Peninsula, written in the 2nd and 1st centuries BC.

familias/idiomas:galata/nota.texto: Celtic language of central Anatolia, known only from names and glosses.

familias/idiomas:britonico/nota.texto: The Celtic language of ancient Britain, from which Welsh, Cornish and Breton descend (which on the map have their own families).

familias/idiomas:picto/nota.texto: Language of the Picts of northern Scotland, known only from names and a few inscriptions. Today most scholars consider it Brittonic; Jackson (1955) thought it was in part non-Indo-European.

familias/idiomas:lusitano/nota.texto: Indo-European language of western Iberia, with a handful of inscriptions from the 1st and 2nd centuries. Whether it is Celtic is debated.

familias/idiomas:iberico/nota.texto: Non-Indo-European language of eastern and southern Iberia; its scripts can be read but the texts are not understood.

familias/idiomas:tartesio/nota.texto: Language of the southwestern stelae of the peninsula. Koch (2009 and later) reads it as Celtic; most scholars leave it unclassified.

familias/idiomas:aquitano/nota.texto: Language of the Aquitani of the Roman period, known from names in Latin inscriptions; related to the ancestor of Basque.

familias/idiomas:tirsenicas/nota.texto: Etruscan, Raetic and the language of the Lemnos stele, which are non-Indo-European.

familias/idiomas:retico/nota.texto: Language of the central and eastern Alps, written between the 5th and 1st centuries BC.

familias/idiomas:ligur/nota.texto: Poorly known language of northwestern Italy and southeastern France; whether it was Indo-European, and whether it was close to Celtic, is debated.

familias/idiomas:venetico/nota.texto: Indo-European language of northeastern Italy, close to the Italic languages.

familias/idiomas:tracio/nota.texto: Indo-European languages with almost no texts, from the eastern Balkans and Dacia. Whether Dacian was a dialect of Thracian is debated.

familias/idiomas:ilirio/nota.texto: Language or languages of the western Balkans, known only from names.

familias/idiomas:frigio/nota.texto: Indo-European language of central Anatolia, related to Greek, written from the 8th century BC to the 3rd century AD.

familias/culturas:neolitica-europea/nota.texto: The first farmers of Europe, who descended mostly from those of Anatolia, and their successors until the Bronze Age.

familias/culturas:campaniforme/nota.texto: Archaeological phenomenon of around 2800-1800 BC. Whether it was a people, a fashion or an exchange network is debated; in Britain it coincides with a large population replacement.

familias/culturas:cordada/nota.texto: Culture of around 2900-2300 BC in northern and central Europe, with a great deal of Steppe ancestry.

familias/culturas:hallstatt/nota.texto: Archaeological culture of the Early Iron Age of central Europe (around 800-450 BC). It is usually linked with the ancestors of the Celts, but that relationship is inferred, not documented.

familias/culturas:picta/nota.texto: Included as a Celtic culture because its language seems Brittonic; this is debated.

familias/culturas:golasecca/nota.texto: Culture of northern Italy (9th to 4th centuries BC) whose people wrote Lepontic, a Celtic language.

familias/culturas:castrena/nota.texto: Culture of the castros of northwestern Iberia. Whether it was Celtic is debated: that is why it is not within the Celtic family.

familias/religiones:religion-iberica/not.texto: Known almost only from sanctuaries and ex-votos: the Iberian texts are not understood.
